kozy-antwerp.name: Kozy Antwerp
kozy-antwerp.tagline: The site of a short-stay property management company in Antwerp: WordPress to Next.js without SEO loss, back office and booking engine
kozy-antwerp.role: I replaced Kozy Antwerp's aging WordPress site with a trilingual Next.js platform. It brings together an owner-facing showcase built to convert, a property back office, and a booking engine (admin validation, Stripe) whose rules are enforced in the database. I started with the PRD and a decision log with the client, then shipped to kozyantwerp.be in two months (217 commits, 46 migrations).

meta.title: Kozy Antwerp · Case study
meta.description: Production site for a short-stay property manager: WordPress cutover without SEO loss, back office, and DB-enforced booking.

paragraphs: Kozy Antwerp manages short stays and B&Bs in Antwerp on behalf of owners. Its WordPress/Elementor site missed the point: in ten seconds, an owner must understand that Kozy handles everything and want a yield estimate. That sentence became the PRD job-to-be-done. Every showcase section was judged against it.

Hard constraint: replace an already indexed site without breaking old URLs. Google history had to survive cutover, with a rollback plan that kept WordPress for at least seven days. Concretely: 52 addresses to remap (property pages, Dutch legal pages, a yield simulator, a stay. booking subdomain) plus WordPress noise (wp-login, wp-admin, feeds, MetForm, empty categories).

Behind the showcase, the team needed a real tool: property CRUD, calendars, weekday/weekend/event pricing, booking requests, admin validation, Stripe and transactional email. Not a generic CMS. A CMS manages content; Kozy needed business rules: who can book which dates, at what price, how long a pending request blocks the calendar, and what happens to guest data after checkout.

I started with the PRD and a 20-decision log (D01-D20) before code. Jira KA-xx tickets, named branches, master/prod and develop/staging. First commit 30 Aug 2026: design system and legal pages. Same day: product docs. Structural choices became ADRs: admin auth and properties (ADR-005), public booking (ADR-006), URLs without language prefix (ADR-008).

Critical invariants live in Postgres and are covered with pgTAP: no double booking under load (pg_advisory_xact_lock, 48h soft-block, exclusion constraint), pending → accepted → confirmed, GDPR anonymization 30 days after checkout. Why in the database? UI rules protect nothing if someone hits the API directly, and races are only fixed at transaction level. Guests never write to bookings: a Zod-validated Server Action calls a single RPC (create_public_booking) with service_role.

Assumed trade-off: one feature flag cuts booking navigation, URLs and server actions. The client could ship the showcase while Stripe stayed in test. Not display:none: when off, navigation is filtered, booking URLs redirect to Collection, create returns booking_disabled and payment checkout_disabled server-side.

context.title: Product context
paragraphs: Personas by priority: Dutch-speaking owners, French-speaking owners, international guests. Internally, Kozy uses the admin panel (Supabase Auth, pending promotion to admin). The panel URL is configurable; its internal path returns 404.

Guests have no account. They pick a property, open a calendar modal that keeps its own URL, enter dates (1-30 nights, earliest check-in tomorrow, Brussels time) and identity, then see “Request recorded, reply within 48h”. A signed HMAC cancel link (14 days) works until payment. After confirmation, a pre-arrival email sends access details the day before.
Out of v1: guest accounts, OTA iCal sync (KA-48 unmerged), blog, analytics (D12: no trackers, so no cookie banner).

Primary CTA (“Calculate my yield”) goes to contact while the flag is off. Old WordPress “gratis-simulatie” redirects to /contact?intent=yield. Contact uses a Resend Server Action with honeypot, rate limit and Reply-To to the prospect (KA-26).

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: Front: Next.js 16 App Router. proxy.ts translates localized public URLs (no /en/ prefix), applies WordPress 301/410s and the booking flag, including Flight soft-nav and Server Actions. Flat routes; proxy rewrites /start (NL) or /accueil (FR). Intercepted booking modal route: modal from Collection, full page from a shared link. Brand motion (panels, FLIP) via GSAP.

Back: Server Actions + Zod, four API routes (two crons, Stripe webhook, llms.txt). Sensitive logic in SECURITY DEFINER RPCs with locked search_path and role grants, verified by pgTAP definer_hardening_catalog. Stripe Checkout hosted; React Email NL/FR/EN via Resend. Webhook stores stripe_events and pays only through mark_booking_paid_guards.

Data: 46 SQL migrations. WebP Storage. Staging staging.kozyantwerp.be (Vercel auth + noindex), prod kozyantwerp.be. Only master/develop deploy. Public calendar never reads bookings: an RPC returns date ranges only, no PII.
bullets: 133 Vitest, 4 Playwright booking specs, database pgTAP tests
10 email templates × 3 languages plus 2 shared components and a dev preview page
Crons: daily pre-arrival, weekly PII purge
52 WordPress URLs as 301s, WP noise as 410s
Trilingual sitemap, hreflang, JSON-LD, llms.txt, robots without admin slug leak
Weekday/weekend/event pricing computed in SQL (pgTAP compute_stay_total)
Prod headers: HSTS preload, X-Frame-Options DENY, CSP frame-ancestors none

decisions.title: Key decisions
paragraphs: Path to “no double booking” in three steps on 19 Oct. Exclusion constraint only covered accepted/confirmed, so pending could overlap a confirmed stay. Fix 1: explicit pre-insert check aligned with the public calendar, locked by pgTAP. Then the race: two requests at the same millisecond both pass “does a booking exist?” before either writes, creating N pending requests and N emails. Added pg_advisory_xact_lock per property so creates serialize; concurrency + soft-block e2e followed. Inclusive range keeps checkout day free for turnover.

SEO migration: CSV of 52 URLs, 301s in next.config with proxy fallback, 410 for wp-login/admin/feeds, redirects for .com/www/stay. Cutover runbook in nine steps (content freeze, tagged deploy, smoke, DNS, TLS, multilingual smoke, sitemap, 301 sample, done). 301 vs 410 is intentional. Lighthouse baseline 25/10: SEO 100.

Security day (19/10, 36 commits) from a defensive audit (0 critical, 7 P2, 12 P3), KA-47. F-01: admin only guarded in proxy; next-action could bypass → RSC layout guard + POST-only. F-07: anon could read bookings via REST/Realtime → policy removed, calendar via date-only RPC. F-12: column revoke useless with table GRANT → revoke table, grant public columns only. Same day: security headers, account enumeration protection, email redaction in logs, signed cancel links, fail-closed real IP on Vercel.
bullets: URLs without language prefix (ADR-008) with coherent hreflang/canonicals
Flag D20 / KA-59: one variable cuts navigation, URLs and Checkout
Admin validation before payment: a business requirement
GDPR: idempotent purge_booking_guest_pii(30), service_role only, weekly cron

execution.title: Delivery and next steps
paragraphs: 30-31 Aug: design system, GSAP nav, legal pages, PRD, hero/panels. September: Services, FLIP Collection, booking modal, WebP; contact demo 30/09. 2-7 Oct: back office, Auth. 9 Oct: first booking in DB, secure RPC, archivable properties, Playwright on both modal variants. 13 Oct: SEO crawlability. 16 Oct: moderation, Stripe, React Email, rate limit, honeypot, 48h expiry, AVIF. 18 Oct: pricing, pre-arrival. 19 Oct: security day + concurrency lock (KA-13). 24-25 Oct: booking hidden (KA-59), prefixless URLs (KA-61), JSON-LD (KA-60), Resend leads (KA-26), Checkout blocked. 27 Oct 2026: staging noindex, final WP redirects, hero videos, prod kozyantwerp.be.

Numbers: 217 commits (31 merges), 15 Jira tickets KA-13 to KA-62, ~54k source lines + ~7.7k tests, Lighthouse staging Perf 83 / SEO 100 / A11y 100 / BP 96. Also 18 pages, ~236 components, 46 migrations, 133 Vitest files, 4 Playwright specs, pgTAP tests, 24 docs. Live 30/10: four properties, 21 sitemap URLs, wp-login 410, .com/www → kozyantwerp.be.

Honesty: booking and Stripe not public yet (client choice). No GitHub Actions CI (Husky + Vercel builds). Engine is ready: flipping one variable opens it. Perf 83 is mostly hero videos. iCal sync exists on a branch waiting for direct booking. Next: open booking, CI, KA-48, hero perf.

spill-crumb.name: Spill The Crumb
spill-crumb.tagline: An anonymous realtime gossip social network, built as a real product: live feed across tabs, DB-enforced anti-spam, back office and 638 automated tests
spill-crumb.role: Spill The Crumb is a community feed where people share and comment on “crumbs” without exposing their identity. I built it as a product ready to grow, not a demo. The feed updates live across tabs; every reaction shows instantly then reconciles with the server; critical rules (anti-spam, counters, notifications) live in Postgres. Around that: CI with E2E on a real local DB, load tests, in-house observability, ADRs and a client guide. Totals: 230 commits, 45 SQL migrations, 638 tests, Lighthouse 97/100 performance on public pages.

meta.title: Spill The Crumb · Case study
meta.description: Anonymous gossip social network: realtime feed, DB anti-spam, CI E2E and 638 tests.

paragraphs: Classic social networks attach every post to a public identity. For a private confidence or small drama, people want a place to post without exposing their name, while a real community still reacts, comments and surfaces what is hot.

Two day-one problems: spam (without a public reputation to protect, someone can fire a hundred posts a minute via the API) and consistency (the same post lives in the feed, profile and detail; if a like updates only one of three screens, the app feels broken).
The product also had to be operable by someone else: dashboard, sponsored slots editable without a developer, readable error log and a user guide. A working feed was not enough.

Guiding principle: every rule that protects the product must hold even if the UI is bypassed. Anti-spam, real post authorship, like/comment counters and notifications are enforced by triggers and RLS. Counters live in post_stats: readable by clients, never writable; only triggers update them.
Code is feature-first (16 domains under features/). app/ only routes; components/ is pure UI. Every Server Action goes through next-safe-action: one wrapper for auth + Zod.

Structural choices as ADRs: single proxy for auth and locale (ADR-001), separate stores with sync (ADR-002), i18n without URL prefix (ADR-003). Tests arrived with features: week one CI already ran authenticated E2E on local Supabase.

context.title: Product context
paragraphs: Member journey: multi-step signup, onboarding, then the feed. Publish a crumb with category and image (iPhone HEIC accepted and converted), react, comment (desktop panel / mobile sheet), follow notifications. Profile shows posts and stats.
Top drama highlights the hottest post. Score: likes - dislikes + 2 × comments. A comment counts twice a like because it signals real engagement.

Ops: stats dashboard, sponsored slot CRUD, platform log and reports. UI in FR/EN/ES without URL prefix. Sponsors do not pay online: slots are created manually in admin to validate the model without payments.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: Front: Next.js 16, Server Components by default. Post state lives in three Zustand stores (paginated feed, profile, detail). GSAP respects prefers-reduced-motion.

Back: typed Server Actions and an internal log ingest route. Heavy logic in SQL: 45 migrations (schema, RLS, counter/notification triggers, Top drama / admin stats / username RPCs, indexes). proxy.ts refreshes the session, resolves locale and assigns a correlation id per request.
Observability: platform_log_events on /admin/logs, auto-purged (30 days platform, 14 days perf) by a scheduled GitHub workflow via service_role.
bullets: 16 pages, 16 domains, ~260 components, ~40k useful lines (cloc)
638 tests in ~200 Vitest files, plus Playwright E2E
Two-job CI: audit, lint, type-check, covered tests, build; then E2E on seeded local Supabase
App rate limits: login 10/15m, signup 5/h, reactions 30/m, comments 10/m, search 60/m
Dedicated load scripts for each limit
Strict TypeScript: 0 any, 0 ts-ignore, generated DB types

decisions.title: Key decisions
paragraphs: Anti-spam that almost never shipped. 5 posts/day is a BEFORE INSERT trigger that also checks the declared author is the authenticated user (POST_AUTHOR_MISMATCH), even via REST. During development I disabled it with a TODO(prod) migration. Risk: ship without anti-spam. Fixed with an explicit re-enable migration (24/06) aligned with POST_DAILY_LIMIT in the app.

One like, three screens, many tabs. ADR-002 compared a global store, refetch, React Query and Context. I kept three specialized stores linked by a sync registry. Mutations fan out to the three stores, BroadcastChannel to other tabs, Supabase Realtime to other users. Optimistic reaction first (+1/-1), then reconcile. Noted debt: every new store must register.

SQL perf: RLS policies rewritten to (select auth.uid()) once per query; Top drama via stored generated drama_level column (Index Scan); username search via pg_trgm; comment pagination via composite index. Storage path bug: first policy misread userId/postId/file (foldername vs filename); fixed then MIME-restricted the bucket.
bullets: ADR-001: single proxy.ts for session and locale
ADR-003: i18n without URL prefix (NEXT_LOCALE cookie + Accept-Language)
Notifications from SQL triggers, no self-notify on own posts
Upstash rate limit with in-memory fallback if unset

execution.title: Delivery and next steps
paragraphs: 6-10 Jun 2026: Next/Supabase/i18n, splash, multi-step auth, feed, publishing, reactions, comments. 11-14 jun: feed optimization, authenticated E2E in CI, profile, detail, cross-tab sync, Top drama. 22-26 jun: notifications, admin, WebP, anti-spam, SEO, sponsoring, logs. 29-30 jun: onboarding, client guide, large refactor (31 commits on 29/06). 10 jul: developer docs. 26-30 oct: audit, Next 16.4.3, P0/P1 remediation, architecture flattening, deploy limited to main.

Late October audit: 26/10 dependency upgrades. 29/10 hardening migration: members can no longer list who liked what (likes readable by author only, counters via post_stats); 18+ and signup fields checked in DB; role/username/birth/gender immutable on profile; SQL limits 10 comments and 30 reactions/hour. Product: reporting, forgot password, export/delete account, keyboard focus and contrast. 30/10: Vercel deploys limited to main.

Numbers: 230 commits (6 Jun → 30 Oct), 16 pages, 45 migrations, 638 tests, ~40k useful lines, ~43 docs including 3 ADRs. Lighthouse public pages: Perf 97, a11y 98-100. Honesty: on a confidences product, anonymity is guaranteed in the database. Next: admin moderation queue, real PWA, shorter splash for signed-in users, EU function region, legal review of terms.

jikowood.name: Jikowood
jikowood.tagline: Showcase and portfolio for a custom carpentry workshop in Brussels: 100+ project photos, three languages, client reviews and local SEO
jikowood.role: A carpentry workshop sells through photos. For this Brussels client I designed and built jikowood.be end to end: a filterable portfolio of 17 custom projects, a page per project, reviews in a database, a contact form and a FR/EN/NL interface. The challenge: serve ~106 HD photos without slowing the site, and be found locally on Google. Live since January 2025, evolved for a year with new jobs (177 commits, 11 reviews, 81 sitemap URLs).

meta.title: Jikowood · Case study
meta.description: Brussels carpentry showcase: photo portfolio, local SEO, i18n and reviews in a database.

paragraphs: Custom carpentry is not a catalog product: it sells craft, proven by real projects. Someone looking for a walk-in closet or TV unit wants concrete interiors before requesting a quote.
Immediate technical problem: a credible portfolio is ~100 HD photos, and heavy photos bounce mobile visitors. The site had to stay fast while showing a lot.

It also had to be found. In Brussels the same prospect may search in French, Dutch or English. Ranking for local queries matters more than a campaign. And the client needed to add reviews without calling me every time.
Built around projects. Home: About, Services, Work, Reviews, Contact. Filterable portfolio and slug pages that are shareable and indexable.
SEO in sprint one: 15 Jan Open Graph, sitemap, robots; 16 Jan dedicated SEO pass. LocalBusiness JSON-LD for local results.
Reviews in MongoDB instead of hardcoding: client adds them without redeploy (1-5 rating, approval status). Projects stay static files: fastest to serve, rarely change.

context.title: Product context
paragraphs: Typical visitor: homeowner with a fit-out project. Arrives from search or a shared link, browses similar work, reads reviews, requests a quote.
Short visual journey: see, trust, contact. Form via Web3Forms, no mail server to maintain.
Basic offline mode (service worker + offline.html), Vercel Analytics and Speed Insights.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: Front: Next.js 14 App Router by screen. framer-motion animations, Swiper carousels. Locale in Zustand, copy in three JSON dictionaries.
Images are the performance core. WebP sources; next/image serves AVIF/WebP with sizes 640-3840. sharp processing, critical CSS via critters, JS bundle splitting.
Back: API route for MongoDB reviews via Mongoose. 17 static projects. HTTPS + HSTS and restrictive security headers.
bullets: 17 projects, ~106 WebP photos, 4 categories
11 reviews via /api/testimonials
81 sitemap URLs (projects × languages)
3 languages: FR, EN, NL
~6,000 lines, ESLint airbnb + jsx-a11y

decisions.title: Key decisions
paragraphs: Client kept seeing an old version after photo updates (browser/CDN/build cache). Fixed 4 Apr in five commits: timestamped generateBuildId, Cache-Control for HTML revalidation, image versioning from March. In hindsight only HTML and replaced images need revalidation; hashed assets can cache for a year.
Keep portfolio richness and optimize the pipeline (WebP, modern formats, responsive sizes, 24h optimized-image cache, lazy load).
Local discovery: LocalBusiness JSON-LD, metadata, Open Graph, hreflang sitemap. SEO passes in February and April.
bullets: Reviews in DB: content without pinging me
Static projects: most viewed content is fastest
Web3Forms: no email infra for a brochure site
Next security bump to 14.2.35 in December 2025

execution.title: Delivery and next steps
paragraphs: 7-16 Jan 2025: initial sprint. February: SEO. March: new projects, image versioning. April: cache, build id, refactor, new photos. May: new job. December 2025: Next security fix and redeploy.
Numbers: 177 commits, 4 pages, 2 API routes, 17 projects, ~106 photos, 11 reviews, 3 languages, 81 sitemap URLs, ~6k lines.

Honesty: first client site in production, maintained a year. What I would strengthen (and a rewrite targets): server title/meta on home, real per-locale URLs so the sitemap stops pointing at 404s, manual review approval, long cache on static assets, TypeScript everywhere, tests and CI.

ttc-v0.name: Take The Crown (3x3)
ttc-v0.tagline: Model the sport before the code, then ship a trustworthy slice
ttc-v0.role: I set the 3x3 product vision (Identity, Competition, Reputation), the domain/architecture documentation, and the MVP implementation: Player/Organizer auth, Geoapify events, verified matches, and World/Country ranking on Next.js + Supabase.

meta.title: Take The Crown 3x3 · Case study
meta.description: 3x3 basketball platform: domain model, Event→Verified→Ranking slice, defense-in-depth AuthZ, and Next.js + Supabase MVP.

paragraphs: The 3x3 ecosystem is split across social networks, organizer sites, registrations, rankings, and chat apps. No single place owns both identity and history.
Without an Event → Match → Verified Result chain, rankings become noise: self-report, unauthorized scores, point farming.
The product must serve players, teams, organizers, and fans without replacing federations: a universal digital layer, not another isolated tournament tool.
Guiding principle: Identity Over Events. Model the sport (actors, competition, ranking) before stacking screens. Documented ≠ Implemented ≠ MVP stays explicit in the docs.
MVP targets the Identity → Event → Match → Result → Ranking → Discovery slice, not a truncated product with no end-to-end value.
Pragmatic stack: Next.js + Supabase monolith (Auth, Postgres+RLS, Storage). No public API or search microservices until data trust is proven.

context.title: Product context
paragraphs: Three pillars: Identity, Competition, Reputation. Ubiquitous language: User, Player, Team, Organization/Organizer, Match, Result, Ranking (≠ Rating ≠ Leaderboard).
Take The Crown 3x3 is distinct from the 1v1 league in the same brand universe: different codebase, different model (multi-events vs 1v1 league).
Docs also cover brackets, circuits, Opportunity, Multi-Tenancy… intentionally broader than shipped code, to guide increments without improvisation.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: Feature-based frontend (auth, create, events, profile, ranking) plus an admin panel behind ADMIN_PANEL_PATH (server rewrite, slug out of the client bundle, profiles.role = admin).
Defense-in-depth AuthZ: Server Actions (requireEventAuthor) + Postgres RLS + author checks inside ranking RPCs, even via service_role.
Events: public creation with mandatory Geoapify address (address, place_id, lat/lng). Public profiles at opaque URLs /profile/[username]-[publicId], public_id ≠ auth.uid.
bullets: Platform MVP roles: player | organizer | admin
Profile UI fork: Player = media gallery; Organizer = Draft/Upcoming/Passed counts
Public Storage buckets (avatars, profile-media) assumed for MVP
Synchronous ranking award via RPC after verified matches

decisions.title: Key decisions
paragraphs: Create = Event only: no Add Score entry in nav. Scores stay reserved to the event author; points only after verified status.
Next + Supabase monolith for MVP velocity: one stack and native RLS; public API and dedicated search engines deferred.
Private events, brackets, OAuth, ELO, livestream, and billing are out of MVP (Under construction UI or absent), even when present in the domain model.
bullets: Score self-report abandoned to protect rankings
In-memory rate-limit acceptable for MVP; Redis later if multi-instance
Browser security policy finalized after asset inventory
List search: soft place_id match or ~1.5 km proximity

execution.title: Execution and next steps
paragraphs: Shipped: email auth Player/Organizer, own-only settings, event CRUD (Geoapify, public), draft→verified matches, W/L points, /ranking World/Country, Player gallery, admin monitoring.
Partial: separate Player domain entity, competition/brackets, full ranking formula (Best 5, event weights, cursor pagination), Registration workflow on the product side.
Live at https://take-the-crown-v001.vercel.app/. Next value: lock useful Registration/brackets and harden ranking before expanding the documented domain further.

enna.name: Enna Consulting
enna.tagline: Trilingual showcase for an HR consultant: one fluid page, but a real URL per section and language to be found and shared in Belgium
enna.role: For a consultant in talent acquisition, diversity and employer branding, I designed a site that explains a three-axis offer in minutes and leads naturally to contact. A Next.js one-pager in FR/NL/EN: single-page fluidity plus 9 real pages for Google (3 languages × 3 sections), each with hreflang and structured data. V1 in 3 days, then refined through the ennabv.be domain (44 commits, 3 PRs).

meta.title: Enna Consulting · Case study
meta.description: Trilingual one-pager for an HR consultant: per-section URLs, international SEO and accessibility.

paragraphs: Enna Consulting helps companies with talent acquisition, diversity & inclusion and employer branding. Audience: SME/ETI leaders and HR teams. The site had to make the offer clear fast, then get people to write.
Belgian constraint: the same prospect may search in NL, FR or EN. A classic one-pager has one URL: weak SEO, and you cannot share “Vision in Dutch”.
First screen: premium calm brand, one contact button. Simple hosting for an independent consultant: no server, no database, no subscription just for a form.
Framed around one goal: turn a visitor into a qualified contact. Non-technical presentation doc versioned with the code.

Single-page comfort with real addresses per section: /fr/home, /nl/about, /en/testimonials. Nine prerendered pages with title, description, canonical, hreflang and social previews. URL updates on scroll without reload; back button stays coherent.
Trade-off: no backend. Browser-validated form via EmailJS. Started with Resend (server route); switched to EmailJS for a fully static site with no server secret.

context.title: Product context
paragraphs: Targets: SME/ETI leaders, HR/TA, growing companies. Out of v1: blog, online booking, client area, analytics.
One repeated CTA: open the contact modal. Dutch default: any URL without a locale redirects there; choice is remembered.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: Front: Next.js 16 catch-all for 9 pages, OnePager assembles sections. IntersectionObserver updates the URL via history.replaceState. Middleware: 308 redirects, 1-year cookie, assets/sitemap/social images pass through.

Back: none. Copy in three translation files. Form RHF + Zod → EmailJS with typed success/error. Documented EmailJS pitfall: empty recipient → 422; config checked up front. Modal: focus trap, scroll lock, portal, success state.
Motion: GSAP for splash only, Framer Motion for modals, Web Animations API for fades.
bullets: 9 static pages + splash + translated 404
hreflang fr-BE / nl-BE / en + x-default, ProfessionalService JSON-LD
OG/Twitter images generated in code
HTTP security headers
~3.5-4k lines, 9 production dependencies

decisions.title: Key decisions
paragraphs: URLs per section instead of # anchors (ignored by Google). April migration + sitemap hreflang. isProgrammaticScroll prevents URL flicker during menu-driven scrolling.
Accessibility as a feature: custom focus-trap hook, screen-reader form errors, splash skipped for prefers-reduced-motion.

Infinite loop bug, step by step. Splash animated then navigated to /home; timeline could restart → endless GET /home. Fix: cancellable timeline (cancel on unmount), navigate once. Shipped 5 minutes after the faulty refactor; same cancel pattern for reduced motion.
Robust site URL: NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL then Vercel prod URL, force https, avoid Search Console duplicates.
bullets: Cancellable GSAP splash: no ghost animations
One Zod schema, small homemade adapter
Open Graph locales fr_BE / nl_BE
No backend: zero server cost, zero server secret

execution.title: Delivery and next steps
paragraphs: 17/02/2026: architecture, i18n, menu, splash (loop bug fixed same night). 18/02: contact, Vision. 19/02: Testimonials, prod ready 0.1. V1 in three days. Then refactors, SEO, EmailJS, ennabv.be, per-locale routes (09/04). Last copy tweak 27/05.
Numbers: 44 commits on 8 active days, 3 PRs, 43 components, 9 pages, 3 languages.
Honesty: prioritized SEO, a11y and the form, shipped fast. Minimal tests (one render test), no CI. Next: route/SEO tests, GitHub Actions, light form anti-spam, client-validated testimonials.

maxweljones.name: Maxwel Jones
maxweljones.tagline: One-page site for a holding that unites an entrepreneur network: an animated Learn / Earn / Return story, a network panel and a two-step contact journey
maxweljones.role: For Maxwel Jones, a holding built around learn, earn, return, I designed a page that tells a vision through scroll. Eight GSAP-animated sections, a side panel of network members, a contact form and a meeting-booking prototype to validate the journey before investing in a real system. After a V1 I refactored into feature modules and documented the choices. 71 commits, live on maxweljones.com.

meta.title: Maxwel Jones · Case study
meta.description: Narrative one-pager for a holding: GSAP storytelling, network panel and two-step contact.

paragraphs: Maxwel Jones is not a one-click product. It is a holding with a Learn / Earn / Return philosophy and a network of people. The site had to make that model clear and desirable, with a premium black-and-gold feel.
First screen had to set identity: letter-by-letter hero, gold bars, header that appears at the right moment.
Show the network without turning the page into a directory, and host two contact modes: Roundtable and consultant meetings later, without complicating the page.
Day 1: Airbnb ESLint + a11y, Prettier, Husky. April 2025 V1 as separate pages.
November 2025: snap-scroll one-pager rewrite. Each section is a module (ui/, hooks/, utils/). Business logic extracted and architecture documented.
Trade-off: meeting booking is a functional prototype (calendar, slots, consultant, confirmation) without persisted reservations, shown as Coming Soon.

context.title: Product context
paragraphs: Audiences: entrepreneurs and partners joining or requesting the network; people discovering the holding.
Eight sections: Hero, About, Philosophy, Learn, Earn, Return, Network, Contact. Contact tabs: Roundtable form and Book a Meeting (weekdays, 15-min slots).
Out of v1: real booking, member area, blog, back office.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: Front: Next.js 15 + React 19. Root layout carries SEO and language/menu/network/animation providers. Page assembles eight modules.
Data: no backend. FR/EN via nested-key t(); members in a typed file; locale stored in the browser.
Calendar isolated in hooks/utils: weekdays, four slots 12:00-12:45. Confirmation injected as a parameter (toast today, API tomorrow). Web3Forms + toast. Hosted on Vercel.
bullets: 8 sections + header, mobile menu, network panel, calendar modal, footer
6 GSAP animation modules
Generated OG image, JSON-LD, sitemap, robots
~4-5k lines, 186 TS/TSX files

decisions.title: Key decisions
paragraphs: Hydration bug, step by step. Server does not know the browser locale. First version read preference immediately → FR HTML vs EN client flash. Fix (23/11): start FR on both sides, apply preference after mount. Side effect: language change restarted the Hero; decoupled on 01/12.
GSAP in gsap.context(), torn down on unmount so ScrollTriggers do not animate dead nodes.
Snap scroll + panel: save and restore read position on close. Unified navigation accounts for header height.
bullets: Rewrite 23/11, logic extraction 02/12, shared components 30/01/2026
Dependency inversion: calendar confirmation as a parameter
ESLint 9 flat config migration

execution.title: Delivery and next steps
paragraphs: 03-09/04/2025: multi-page V1. 23/11: one-page rewrite, snap scroll, hydration, client README. 01-02/12: hero, header, network, menu, logic extraction. 07/12: CVE. 29-30/01/2026: Book a call, ESLint 9, React 19. 01-06/02: About, SEO, Web3Forms, prod.
Numbers: 71 commits on 12 active days, 2 major PRs, 8 sections, 2 languages, 6 animation modules.

Honesty: architecture and UX before tests. No automated tests or CI yet (lint + Husky). Browser-side locale means Google mostly indexes FR. Next: real booking, Vitest for calendar/form, /fr /en routes, real member photos.

nana.name: Hors Cadre
nana.tagline: A premium photo portfolio and the custom private studio that lets the photographer publish albums of hundreds of images on her own
nana.role: A photographer needs two things: a showcase that puts images first, and autonomy to update it without a developer. I built both in four weeks with Next.js 16 and Supabase. Public side: a gallery with crafted transitions. Studio side: a private back office where up to 1,200 photos per batch are converted to WebP in the browser, uploaded with resume, reordered by drag-and-drop and published in one click. Security goes all the way to the database. Totals: 142 commits, 15 PRs, 13 migrations, 142 test files, E2E CI and 15 ADRs.

meta.title: Hors Cadre · Case study
meta.description: Premium photo portfolio and private studio: bulk WebP upload, Supabase RLS, CI and 15 ADRs.

paragraphs: A photographer’s portfolio has one rule: the UI must step aside for the images. No heavy cards, no copy competing with the photo, but transitions that make moving between albums feel valuable. The public site had to be calm, fast and fluid on mobile and desktop.

The real problem was behind the curtain. A shoot easily means hundreds of 10-50 MB files. Generic CMSs struggle, specialized hosts bill storage, and depending on a developer for every album is not viable. The tool had to serve one gesture: drop a whole folder, reorder, pick a cover, publish.
Third constraint: cost. A photo-heavy site can explode egress and transform bills. Every technical choice had to account for the cost of a displayed image.
I documented it as a product: 15 ADRs with context, rejected options and trade-offs, plus a non-jargon vision guide for the client. ADR-001 compares Supabase to Firebase, a custom backend and a CMS.
Team-style Git even solo: feature/*, develop, uat, main, 15 PRs. GitHub Actions CI: lint, tests, build, then Playwright Chromium. Pre-commit: zero ESLint warnings, green tests.
Core idea: move heavy work where it costs least. Photo conversion in the admin browser. Public pages cached. Thumbnails served straight from Supabase Storage, not Vercel’s image optimizer.

context.title: Product context
paragraphs: Two audiences. Visitors browse home, masonry gallery, then each album with a fullscreen viewer. The photographer, sole admin, manages everything from a private studio behind a non-public URL.
Deliberate mono-account model: the trigger refuses a second profile (PROFILE_ALREADY_EXISTS). Less attack surface, no team roles.
Out of v1: client accounts, print sales, comments, Sentry. FR/EN from the browser then cookie, no URL prefix, so album URLs stay simple.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: Front: Next.js 16 Server Components. Public pages revalidate every 300s; studio edits invalidate cache surgically. proxy.ts refreshes the session, isolates admin session, redirects to login with returnTo, no-store on admin.
Back: no REST API. Every mutation is a Server Action in its own folder, always: identity + role, Zod, write, invalidate cache.
Data: albums (title, slug, publish, order, cover, images JSONB) and profiles (admin role). Files at album-photos/albums/{id}/{image}.webp. Cover dimensions denormalized so masonry does not jump.
bullets: 13 SQL migrations, reproducible local DB, generated types
5 RLS policies on albums (public read of published + admin CRUD)
~15 admin Server Actions, one function per file
142 Vitest files + 2 Playwright scenarios
Business limits: 1,200 files/batch, 50 MB/file, 640px thumb q=0.82, 3 retries
~15k app lines and ~7.5k test lines

decisions.title: Key decisions
paragraphs: Upload that resumes where it stopped. Each photo: (1) WebP convert, (2) storage upload, (3) DB record, with a checkpoint after each step. source_fingerprint skips duplicates if the same folder is dropped again.

The disappearing photos bug. Images live in one JSONB. Add = read, append, write. Parallel uploads meant two requests read the same version and the second write erased the first. Fix: serialize the queue (ALBUM_UPLOAD_CONCURRENCY = 1) + dedupe. Integrity before speed. Next: atomic SQL append to restore parallelism.

Security layers: configurable admin URL (≥16 chars or 404), proxy for guests, assertAdminMutation on every action, Postgres RLS. Linter flagged is_admin() as SECURITY DEFINER: fixed by migration, not ignored.
Cost: client WebP (createImageBitmap + canvas), direct Supabase thumbs, egress branch (PR #14), cover dimensions in DB.
bullets: Server Actions over REST (ADR-002)
Images in JSONB (ADR-005): one query per album, documented trade-off
Cover-column fallback fixed a prod 500 on 09/07
GSAP with prefers-reduced-motion (ADR-010), animation logic tested

execution.title: Delivery and next steps
paragraphs: 14-15/06/2026: foundations, design system, GSAP splash, conducting bar, nav, cookie i18n, Vitest. 16/06: CI, a11y, responsive. 20-21/06: gallery, album, cover handoff, viewer, studio shell. 02-03/07: Supabase. 05/07: Server Action hardening, SEO, dnd, ADRs, prod. 08-12/07: uploads, backups, egress, direct thumbs.
Numbers: 142 commits in 29 days (12 active), 15 PRs, 13 migrations, 15 ADRs, 142 test files (~455 tests claimed), 437 TS files and 146 React components.

Honesty: upload reliability before speed, photographer autonomy before extras. k6 (250 VU) ready but not run; Sentry out of v1. Next: atomic append, per-photo alt text, custom domain, k6 run, docs synced to code.

purpose-sport.name: Purpose Sport
purpose-sport.tagline: Site for a basketball player management agency, built as a talent catalog for clubs and partners
purpose-sport.role: For an agency representing basketball players, I built a showcase that explains the mission in a few screens, then presents each player like a recruitment dossier (career, awards, highlight video). Bilingual Next.js one-pager, indexed from launch (metadata, Search Console, auto sitemap), with Analytics and Jest tests per section. V1 in three days, then a full art-direction rewrite. 61 commits, live on purpose-sport.com.

meta.title: Purpose Sport · Case study
meta.description: Basketball management agency showcase: player catalog, video, SEO and Jest tests.

paragraphs: A sports management agency sells trust. A sporting director must quickly see who it represents and why to trust it. Without a credible site it depends on word of mouth and social media.
Core need: the players. A recruiter wants position, career, awards and game footage, fast, without ten tabs.
The site also had to be findable: name on Google, clean social previews.
V1 in three days (16-18/01/2025): nav, hero, about, player accordion, contact. Goal: something concrete to discuss.

23/03/2025: hard call to delete everything and restart. The accordion hid players. Rebuild around a central Players section (card + video) and objective cards, then new art direction in early April. Restarting cost less than bending the old code.
Content separated from code: players in typed data/data.ts. Adding a player is an entry. Jest tests what users see (active player, pagination, player), not implementation details.

context.title: Product context
paragraphs: Audiences: club recruiters and sporting directors, partners/sponsors, then players and families.
One page, six blocks: Hero, About, Objectives, Players, Contact, Footer. Horizontal nav follows scroll and hides near the form.
Out of v1: player area, per-player indexable pages, live stats, back office. Content edited in code, reasonable for ~10 profiles.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: Layout: full SEO (OG, Twitter, canonical, robots, Search Console, manifest), three next/font faces, Analytics, i18n and scroll providers.
Players: active card (career, awards, video) + paginated list of 6. react-player via dynamic ssr:false for light first paint and no hydration issues.
Contact: five a11y-labeled fields via Web3Forms. No database: players, videos and translations ship with the site. Sitemap/robots regenerated postbuild.
bullets: 1 page, 6 sections, 2 languages (EN default)
11 profiles (10 shown), 3 highlight videos
6 Jest files (one per section + navigation)
~5-6k lines including player data and i18n

decisions.title: Key decisions
paragraphs: Restart at the right time. March 2025 V1 worked but contradicted the goal. Delete and rebuild in three days rather than pile patches.
Video without tanking the page: player loaded on demand client-side only.
Scroll-aware nav via shared IntersectionObserver; navbar hides when the form fills the viewport.
bullets: Usage-oriented tests (player, pagination, player)
Content separated from code
SEO from launch (Search Console, next-sitemap)
RSC CVE fix on 23/12/2025 then release 1.0.0

execution.title: Delivery and next steps
paragraphs: 16-18/01/2025: V1. 13/03: animations, skeletons, mobile. 23-25/03: rewrite, objectives, Players+video, Husky, Jest. 04-10/04: desktop/mobile, Analytics, art direction, Search Console, sitemap. 23/12/2025: security fix and release 1.0.0.
Numbers: 61 commits on 13 active days, 6 tests, 20 components, 11 profiles, 2 languages, 1 full rewrite.

Honesty: early-2025 project. Larger components than I write today, videos in the repo, unfinished locale detection. Next: split sections, host videos elsewhere with posters, visible form failure states, CI, per-player indexable pages.
I build web applications starting from usage.

Understand what the user needs, then build the interface, the logic and the rules that go with it, through to launch. I work on products where frontend really matters: booking platforms, back offices, realtime apps and business tools.

productMindset.title: Product mindset
intro: Understand the real need before choosing the technical solution. I decide early, ship a focused first product and keep a readable trajectory.
On Kozy Antwerp, I wrote the specs and a journal of 20 decisions with the client before the first line of code. When payments were not ready, a single switch let us ship the showcase without waiting.
productMindset.outro: Every feature must answer a concrete use case, not fill a checklist.

frontendPhilosophy.title: Frontend philosophy
intro: Frontend sets a product’s rhythm: it makes it feel fast, fluid and obvious. Concretely:
bullets: a reaction that shows instantly, then syncs with the server (Spill the Crumb)
hundreds of photos uploaded at once, with automatic resume if the connection drops (Hors Cadre)
an app that keeps working offline for drivers in the field (FleetScan)
flows designed mobile-first, and usable with a keyboard
frontendPhilosophy.outro: Interfaces that make sense quickly and move without friction.

buildingApplications.title: What I build
intro: Tools built for real uses, with real business logic behind the screen:
bullets: booking platforms with validation, payment and automated emails
custom back offices
realtime applications
installable web apps that work offline
fast showcase sites with solid SEO
buildingApplications.outro: Usage in the field guides what I ship, not the other way around.

technicalApproach.title: Technical approach
intro: Simple architectures, organised in components, with a coherent interface system. I rely on three principles:
bullets: Critical rules live in the database. A double booking or spam cannot bypass them, even if the UI has a bug.
The code is tested. 638 automated tests on Spill the Crumb, and database tests on Kozy.
Decisions are written down. Every architecture choice is documented so the next developer understands why.
technicalApproach.outro: Technology should serve the product, not the other way around.

motionInteraction.title: Motion & interaction
intro: Animation guides the eye and keeps the interface fluid. It never exists for decoration.
motionInteraction.outro: Motion stays discreet and useful, with GSAP, and it turns off for people who prefer reduced motion.

collaborationExecution.title: Collaboration & execution
intro: Clear communication, sharp priorities and visible progress. In practice:
bullets: separate tickets and branches for testing and for production
a check on a staging environment before every launch
a client kept in the loop with plain words, not jargon
autonomy, without losing the frame
collaborationExecution.outro: Move clearly, all the way to launch.

closing.label: In short
paragraphs: I like turning a fuzzy need into a clear, reliable product that feels good to use, and shipping it end to end.
